title: Cyclically Rotating a Grid
description:
You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `grid`, where both `m` and `n` are even integers, and a positive integer `k`.

The matrix consists of `min(m, n) / 2` concentric rectangular layers. In one cyclic rotation, every element in every layer moves one position **counter-clockwise** along its own layer (the top edge shifts left, the left edge shifts down, the bottom edge shifts right, and the right edge shifts up).

Return the resulting matrix after performing `k` counter-clockwise cyclic rotations.
constraints: Both m and n are even integers.
hints: Each concentric layer is completely independent and has its own perimeter length L.
Extract each layer in clockwise order into a 1D list; rotating counter-clockwise by k corresponds to shifting that list left by (k % L) positions.

examples.explanation: In a 2x2 grid, one counter-clockwise shift moves 40 down, 30 right, 20 up, and 10 left.
The outer layer of length 12 shifts counter-clockwise by 2 and the inner 2x2 layer of length 4 shifts counter-clockwise by 2.
A 2x4 grid has a single layer of length 8; rotating by k = 8 returns the exact original grid.
